public_context.instructions: Select one RISC-V custom instruction, or the unchanged baseline. Maximize VERIFIED FEASIBLE whole-program speedup within the measurement-attempt budget. Predictions are uncalibrated, not measurements. Consider the factorized decision score, pairwise rank, public workload features, paid outcomes, hardware constraints and measurement cost. Use only list_candidates, predict, measure and finalize. Every submitted measure request, including an invalid ID or repeat, consumes an attempt; failed measurements also count. No unqueried outcome is available. Only the current incumbent may be finalized: use incumbent.candidate_id exactly, or use null only when incumbent.candidate_id is null. The host computes the best paid, correct, device-fitting, area/timing-feasible improvement; never finalize a stale, unmeasured, infeasible, or lower-speedup candidate. Check remaining.decision_turns_after_this_response and provider_calls_available_including_this_response. Each provider response permits one tool action; reserve a later call to finalize after a measurement. If the remaining decision/provider allowance is exhausted, the host selects its verified incumbent or baseline. You may stop early. Every measure action must include a concise public-evidence decision_summary of at most 320 characters. If routing_review is present, review the primary proposal against the public evidence and utility recommendation before returning the action you support. Do not provide private chain of thought. The final summary you submit is an unverified agent note; the host returns the authoritative measured result. Single instructions only; individual speedups and area cannot be added. This is a prospective live hardware-measurement session on a new workload group. The target source and exact operator-tree families are excluded from training; this is one full original 8,215-case nanocobs differential probe and does not establish broad workload generalization. Each measure action triggers one real, one-attempt target evaluation. The request may include current_grouped_ml_bundle metadata. When present, the predict tool returns pairwise_rank_score (an ordering score, not a speedup estimate), pairwise_rank_position, factorized_feasibility_probability and factorized_decision_score for the 64-LUT4 cap. Feasibility scores and their ensemble disagreement are uncalibrated; disagreement is not a confidence interval. A selection_board appears after predict and separates the frozen pairwise order, analytic latency estimate, uncalibrated feasibility-like signals and paid verification. The board separately names the highest pairwise-ranked candidate and the unattempted candidate with the highest frozen factorized decision score. Use the utility recommendation as the default next measurement unless a paid observation or specific public evidence supports an override. Do not choose by raw feasibility score alone. When overriding, state the recommended candidate, the alternative, their relative decision-score ratio, and the evidence that justifies the tradeoff in decision_summary. Never infer area or feasibility from operation count or any uncalibrated score. The factorized score is an ordering proxy made from an uncalibrated feasibility signal times the nonnegative public analytic cycle-reduction estimate; it is not a calibrated expected value. Only a paid outcome verifies area, timing and correctness.

actual_dataset_collection.scope: full-pool corpus/oracle collection; costs every actual pool member once, irrespective of replay budget

policy_costs_note: Each non-agent policy is replayed with one-at-a-time outcome release and counts only its own B1/B2/B3 prefix. Those are offline counterfactual decision costs on already collected target labels; actual corpus construction measured the complete pool.

source_family_audit.interpretation: Exact operation-tree families are excluded from training. A binary-framing probe and exact-family holdout are descriptive; recent public pools must also be audited before independence claims.

limitations: The Codex bridge uses the active chat model with broader workspace tools available; it is a cooperative relay, not a security sandbox.
Exact model ID, token usage and model-only latency are unavailable for the chat bridge.
Only one LLM episode is planned; it is exploratory, not a multi-seed agent-quality estimate.
The workload is binary-framing fixed-probe transfer, not independent-family confirmation.
The current dataset contains no combined-instruction outcomes; selections are single instructions.
Scalar reference includes the same pinned cobs.c with renamed symbols and SWAR disabled; differential agreement cannot exclude shared source bugs.
The complete timed probe includes its scalar reference and checker; this is not standalone codec throughput.
Only one new fixed-probe source and one Codex-agent episode are included.
Candidate measurements will be collected to build an oracle; only charged per-policy prefixes count toward selector budgets.
Hardware timing is FPGA synthesis/routing on the established toolchain, not silicon measurement.
Individual-instruction results do not establish multi-instruction composition.
One fixed nanocobs source and differential probe are not sufficient to establish broad workload generalization; exact operation-tree-family holdout is also a stricter, narrower transfer test.
The LLM result is one current-chat relay episode without an available deployment ID, provider tokens or isolated API execution.
Five ML seeds are dependent algorithm runs on one candidate pool, not independent workload replicates.
An unresolved or infrastructure-censored outcome makes exhaustive-oracle speedup and regret unavailable; conclusively incorrect candidates are disqualified as infeasible.
This study evaluates individual instructions; it does not test combined instruction sets or full processor implementation of selected combinations.
